content: Brief reactive psychosis is characterized by a sudden and short-term onset of psychotic behavior, such as hallucinations or delusions, typically triggered by a stressful event. Symptoms of Brief Reactive Psychosis: Individuals may exhibit disorganized behavior. They may experience delusions, which are false beliefs about what is happening around them. Hallucinations, such as hearing or seeing things that are not real, can occur. Speech or language may become unusual or strange. These symptoms are not caused by alcohol or drug abuse. They persist for more than a day but resolve within less than a month. Causes of Brief Reactive Psychosis: This condition is often triggered by extreme stress, such as a traumatic accident or the loss of a loved one. After the episode, individuals typically return to their previous level of functioning. The affected person may or may not recognize their behavior as unusual. It most commonly affects individuals in their 20s, 30s, and 40s. Those with personality disorders are at a higher risk of developing this condition. When to Seek Urgent Medical Care: If you experience symptoms of this disorder, it is important to schedule an appointment with a mental health professional. If there are concerns about your safety or the safety of others, contact local emergency services (e.g., 911) or go to the nearest emergency room immediately. Diagnosis: A psychiatric evaluation is necessary to confirm the diagnosis. A physical examination and laboratory tests may be conducted to rule out medical conditions as the cause of the symptoms. Treatment Options: By definition, psychotic symptoms resolve on their own within less than one month. However, in some cases, brief reactive psychosis may be the initial presentation of a more chronic psychotic condition, such as schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder. Antipsychotic medications can help reduce or eliminate psychotic symptoms. Talk therapy can assist in coping with the emotional stress that triggered the episode. Where to Find Medical Care: Seek directions to hospitals or facilities that specialize in treating brief reactive psychosis. Prognosis: Most individuals with this condition have a favorable outcome. However, repeat episodes may occur in response to future stress. Possible Complications: Like all psychotic illnesses, this condition can significantly disrupt an individual’s life. It may also lead to violence or suicide in severe cases.
